messages:
alex: CI on main is red for PR #5342 — matrix linux-py38 axis=3 failing 4/6 tests. Build step passed, tests failed. Can someone do a minimal retrigger that skips image rebuild and only reruns the pytest step? I don't want to waste capacity on a full rebuild.
sam: @alex can you paste the failed job link + run id?
alex: https://ci.example.com/runs/7654321 matrix job: run/7654321/axis=3 commit abc1234
infra-bot: Noted. You can use our lightweight retry helper: `./dev/ci retry --run-id=7654321 --axis=3 --stage=tests --no-rebuild` Example:
```
./dev/ci retry --run-id=7654321 --axis=3 --stage=tests --no-rebuild
# or via gh actions: gh run rerun 7654321 --name matrix-linux-py38-axis3
```
maria: FYI that helper preserves the build cache and reuses wheel cache, but it won't rehydrate secrets if the failure was auth-related.
alex: running now...
alex: ./dev/ci retry --run-id=7654321 --axis=3 --stage=tests --no-rebuild
ci-bot: queued lightweight rerun for run 7654321 axis=3 (no image rebuild). CI job 7654321-rerun-1 created.
sam: I'll keep an eye — if it flakes again we can bisect or force the single test via `pytest -k test_timeout_handler` on the artifact.
jess: rerun finished, still failing on test_timeout_handler::test_retry_scheduling — same trace as before. Attaching last 50 lines:
```
E   assert 200 == 500
...
TimeoutError: task exceeded 30s
```
alex: sounds like a legit test failure. I'll add a quick PR to increase timeout and run a full matrix if it passes.
maria: For future, when it's an intermittent runtime timeout consider `--isolated` runner or bumping the test's wait to avoid noisy flakes. Also add `@flake-monitor` tag if you want auto-retry.
alex: thanks all. reopening if rerun shows green. :thumbsup:
